messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — running the nightly flash/paged fusion sweep and hit a regression when enabling the tiled pipeline + smem fusion path on A100.
maya: ugh, details? perf numbers? :thinking:
alex: short summary: when tile=64 + pipeline=3 we see ~10% p99 uplift and gpu_sm_eff drops ~5%. throughput also dips a bit for batch sizes >=8. reproducer below.
alex: ```
# repro command
./run_bench --model flash-paged-fused --tile 64 --pipeline 3 --batch 8 --kv-prefetch on

# perf summary
model: flash-paged-fused
config: tile=64 pipeline=3 batch=8 kv_prefetch=on
p50: 27.4ms -> 29.1ms (+6.2%)
p99: 85ms -> 94ms (+10.6%)
throughput: 710 -> 658 tokens/s (-7.3%)
gpu_sm_eff: 72% -> 67%
mem-bandwidth-util: 78% -> 84%
``` 
chris: interesting — mem-bandwidth-util up while sm_eff down suggests more stalls waiting for DRAM, maybe shared-memory bank conflicts or suboptimal tiling causing extra global traffic.
maya: did you capture nvprof traces? any divergent warps or long global mem ops?
alex: yes, attached a short nvprof flame (trimmed). hotspots show more L2 misses on KV loads on pipelined lanes; smem stores seem more serialized. suspect the tiled kernel's pipeline stage ordering interacts badly with our KV prefetcher when tile size is 64.
sam: have we tried smaller tiles? 32 or 48 often help occupancy vs smem tradeoff.
alex: tried tile=32 pipeline=3 -> p99 back to 86ms, throughput 700. sm_eff 70%, mem-bandwidth 79% (closer to baseline). so tile=64 is the problem region.
maya: can you paste the kernel launch params? occupancy numbers?
alex: ```
launch: block=(256,1,1) threads=256 warps=8
shared_mem_per_block: 64KB
registers_per_thread: 64
estimated_occupancy: 1.5 blocks/SM (low)
``` 
chris: occupancy 1.5 blocks/SM is low for A100 — with tile=64 smem per block spikes so we can't schedule enough blocks -> underutilized SMs and more global mem bursts.
sam: maybe pipeline=2 would reduce in-flight stages and lower smem pressure.
maya: also curious about KV cache behavior: prefix batch mixing can cause strided KV reads, increasing L2 misses. Are we merging prefix KV properly per-batch?
alex: current batching heuristic merges prefixes only if total_kv_size < kv_merge_threshold (set to 128MB). In this benchmark with batch=8 some prefixes exceed the threshold so we do per-request KV loads -> more random DRAM reads.
chris: lowering kv_merge_threshold helps but increases memory copy cost and might regress latency for lower-sequence workloads.
alex: proposed quick fixes:
- reduce tile -> 32 for A100 baseline
- try pipeline=2 for tile=64 test to see smem pressure effect
- tweak kv_merge_threshold to 96MB for prefetched workloads
- add small circular prefetch buffer to smooth KV reads (idea)

maya: i'll run a quick matrix: tile=[32,48,64], pipeline=[2,3], kv_merge=[96,128] and post numbers in ~30m.
dev-bot: perf-run started for matrix (id=pr-1865432100) at 1865432140
maya: preliminary numbers: tile=48 pipeline=2 kv_merge=96 looks promising: p99 88ms, throughput 695, sm_eff 71%, mem-bandwidth 80%.
sam: nice. can we try a micro-optim: pack KV layout to reduce L2 miss stride for the common prefix sizes?
chris: also add a small test with contiguous-kv-layout flag on — the fusion path prefers that layout.
alex: thanks team. i'll push a short PR to add pipeline=2 as safe fallback when tile>=64 and sm_eff dips below 68% (heuristic). also will instrument more counters: L2_miss_per_kv_load and smem_bank_conflict_events.
maya: sounds good. logging idea: emit a perf-tag when we switch kernels automatically so we can backtrace regressions later.
alex: agreed. I'll include perf-tag in rollout. will circle back after the matrix completes.
dev-bot: perf-run pr-1865432100 completed at 1865432175 (results uploaded to /perf/artifacts/pr-1865432100)
chris: thumbs up. follow-up: add a short oncall playbook entry — if deploy triggers >7% p99 regression in flash-paged-fused, auto-fallback to tile=32/pipeline=2 for 10 minutes.
sam: I'll draft the playbook.
maya: Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
